post.caption:
Pluto never moved and never shrank. It stopped being a planet because a room of astronomers in Prague changed what the word means.

One science fact a day. Follow so you don't miss tomorrow's.

#pluto #planets #solarsystem #space #astronomy #science #eris #dwarfplanet #spacefacts #sciencefacts #didyouknow

subject_anchor: the solar system and the people who study it: planets, moons, orbits, telescopes, star charts, observatories and the night sky
style_lock: detailed hand-drawn ink and pencil illustration, fine varied line weight, careful cross-hatching and stippling for shading, realistic proportions and believable material texture, sparing muted colour washes over mostly monochrome ink, visible paper grain, generous negative space, one clear focal subject

beats.text: Pluto never moved, never shrank, and still stopped being a planet.
beats.image_prompt: a small cratered grey world sitting alone on a low museum pedestal beneath a dark domed ceiling of painted stars, its name plaque already unscrewed and lying face up on the floor beside it

beats.text: For seventy six years it was the ninth dot on every classroom poster.
beats.image_prompt: seen from the back of an empty classroom, a curling paper chart of nine planets in a tall column taped above a chalk tray, the smallest one at the bottom peeling away from the wall

beats.text: Then astronomers found Eris, further out than Pluto and slightly heavier.
beats.image_prompt: a close overhead view of a glass photographic sky plate pinned under two fingertips, a dense field of stars across it and one faint dot ringed in fresh ink, a cold half drunk mug at the frame edge

beats.text: So either we had a tenth planet, or the word planet meant nothing.
beats.image_prompt: a chalkboard seen at a slight angle carrying nine chalk planets drawn in a neat column, a tenth added below them in a smaller hesitant hand, chalk dust heaped along the rail

beats.text: It had never actually been defined.
beats.image_prompt: a close overhead view of a heavy open dictionary on a desk beside a brass orrery, one entry left as empty ruled space, a magnifying glass resting across the blank line

beats.text: So in two thousand six, astronomers finally wrote the rules.
beats.image_prompt: an open notebook propped on a windowsill at night showing three short empty ruled boxes, a telescope standing silhouetted against the stars through the glass behind it

beats.text: Orbit the Sun. Be round. Sweep your own lane clean.
beats.image_prompt: three small drawn panels stacked in a vertical column, the top a planet looping around a sun, the middle a round world beside a drafting compass, the bottom a worn broom pushing rocks out of a curved orbit track

beats.text: Pluto passes the first two easily.
beats.image_prompt: a close view of two weathered hands holding a small round world up against the night sky, checking its curve against a circle drawn on a sheet of tracing paper

beats.text: But its orbit is crowded with thousands of icy chunks it never cleared.
beats.image_prompt: a far overhead view of a wide crowded belt of thousands of tiny icy rocks, one slightly larger round world pushing through the middle of them and leaving no gap behind it

beats.text: So a few hundred astronomers in a hall in Prague raised their hands.
beats.image_prompt: seen from the very back row of a packed lecture hall, a field of small raised hands above the seat backs, a huge projected photograph of a distant icy world glowing on the far wall

beats.text: Pluto did not change that day. Our definition did.
beats.image_prompt: a macro view of a pencil eraser being lifted away from a notebook page where one word is half rubbed out, a small untouched pencil sketch of a ringed planet still intact beside it, eraser crumbs scattered

beats.text: And every planet still on that list is stranger than the one we removed.
beats.image_prompt: a tall vertical column of eight planets seen edge on against open sky, one tipped fully onto its side, one wearing a broad flat ring, one marked with a single huge swirling storm
